text:
In this activity, we will consider some simple examples that will guide us in finding a more general approach.

Give a description of the solution space to the linear system: $$ \begin{alignedat}{3} x \amp = \amp 2 \\ y \amp = \amp -1. \\ \end{alignedat} $$

$(x,y) = (2,-1)$.

The equations tell us the value of both variables so there is only one solution $(x,y) = (2,-1)$.

Give a description of the solution space to the linear system: $$ \begin{alignedat}{4} -x \amp {} + {} \amp 2y \amp {}-{} \amp z \amp {}={} \amp -3 \\ \amp \amp 3y \amp {}+{} \amp z \amp {}={} \amp -1 \\ \amp \amp \amp \amp 2z \amp {}={} \amp 4. \\ \end{alignedat} $$

$(x,y,z) = (-1,-1,2)$.

We first use the third equation to determine that $z=2$. We next substitute this value into the first two equations to obtain $$ \begin{alignedat}{3} -x \amp {} + {} \amp 2y \amp {}={} \amp -1 \\ \amp \amp 3y \amp {}={} \amp -3. \\ \end{alignedat} $$ Now we can use the second equation to determine that $y=-1$, substitute that value into the first equation, and determine that $x=-1$. This tells us that the linear system has one solution $(x,y,z) = (-1,-1,2)$.

Give a description of the solution space to the linear system: $$ \begin{alignedat}{3} x \amp {} + {} \amp 3y \amp {}={} \amp -1 \\ 2x\amp {}+{} \amp y \amp {}={} \amp 3. \\ \end{alignedat} $$

$(x,y) = (2,-1)$.

Notice that we can rewrite the first equation as $x=-1-3y$ and substitute this into the second equation to obtain $$ 2(-1-3y)+y = -2 -5y = 3. $$ This tells us that $y=-1$ and $x=-1-3y = 2$. The linear system therefore has one solution $(x,y) = (2,-1)$.

Describe the solution space to the linear equation $0x = 0$.

Any real number is a solution.

No matter the value of $x$, we have $0x = 0$. Therefore, the solution space to the equation $0x=0$ is all real numbers $x$. In other words, this equation does not place a restriction on the value of $x$.

Describe the solution space to the linear equation $0x = 5$.

There are no solutions.

By contrast, the equation $0x=5$ has no solutions since no value of $x$, when multiplied by $0$, can produce $5$.
